entries.content: [when] (b-15) Or omit [when]. Ver. 9 proves this to be probably the true sense.
[them] (c-29) Or 'ye heard and knew.'
minister (d-14) Or 'servant,' diakonos.
filled (e-31) Pleroo, as in v. 25 ('complete'); ch. 2.10 ('complete'); and ch. 4.17 ('fulfil'). knowledge (f-35) Epignosis, i.e. 'full knowledge,' as chs. 2.2; 3.10; Matt. 11.27; Eph. 1.17.
knowledge (f-23) Epignosis, i.e. 'full knowledge,' as chs. 2.2; 3.10; Matt. 11.27; Eph. 1.17.
strengthened (g-1) Lit. 'made powerful with all power.'
portion (h-14) See Note, Acts 26.18.
creation; (i-11) See Note h, ver. 23.

by (k-2) En. Lit. 'in him,' in the power of whose person. He was the one whose intrinsic power characterized the creation. It exists as his creature. things, (l-7) Looked at as a whole. 'the all things,' as vers. 17,20; Eph. 3.9. things (a-33) See Note l ver. 16. by (b-37) Dia, the instrumental power. for (c-40) Eis, 'for.' These three prepositions, en, dia, eis, show Christ to be the characteristic power, the active instrument, and the end in creation.
Godhead] (d-9) I add '[of the Godhead]' from ch. 2.9, as it makes the 'it' in vers. 21, 22 seem less harsh.
by (b-2) Dia, the instrumental power.
it (e-17) i.e. 'the fulness,' ver. 19.
through (b-7) Dia, the instrumental power. it, (e-18) i.e. 'the fulness,' ver. 19. irreproachable (f-16) 'One against whom no charge can be brought,' as Tit. 1.6,7.

the (g-6) Or 'in faith,' that is, full assurance of heart in the gospel. creation (h-33) The word is used either of 'the creation,' or abstractly of 'the creature' as such; once for 'institution,' 1Pet. 2.13. Thus, in ver. 15, it is not of each individual as such, but of everything called 'creation' in its nature. see Heb. 9.11.

Now, (i-1) He had previously become minister (diakonos, vers. 23,25); he was now in prison, but rejoicing in suffering. up (k-11) This refers to what lacked as yet; not to Paul taking 'his turn' as a person, in what is yet lacking.

dispensation (l-9) Or, 'economy,' as 'administration' in 1Cor. 9.17; Eph. 1.10; 3.2,9; 'dispensation,' 1Tim. 1.4; and 'stewardship,' Luke 16.2,3,4. complete (m-19) See Note e, ch. 1.9, also Note, Matt. 5.17.
up (a-4) 'Rooted' is the perfect participle; it speaks of what had been done and continued. 'Built up' is the present, and is continuous. we might say 'being built up.' assured (b-8) Or 'confirmed.'
*you* (c-10) 'You' is emphatic; but the verb 'be' is in the future, implying real present danger more than possibility.

complete (d-4) Pleroo, as ch. 1.9. Or 'filled full,' referring to all fulness being in him. The fulness or completeness of the Godhead is in Christ, as towards us; and we, as towards God, are complete in him. 'Godhead' here is Theotes -- Godhead in the absolute sense -- not Theiotes, merely divine in character.
working (e-19) Energeia. active internal power, as Eph. 1.19; 3.7; 4.16; Phil. 3.21; Col. 1.29.
effaced (f-2) Used for annulling a decree of law; as 'blot out,' Acts 3.19; Rev. 3.5. handwriting (g-4) Handwriting, obligation to which a man is subject by his signature.
it. (h-18) Or 'in him.' In all the preceding passage the antecedent is God (ver. 12).
them].) (i-11) A term of Roman law. a class of objects as to the possession of which there were peculiar rules.

appearance (k-5) Logos. there was something to allege, to say for it. flesh. (l-29) The clause in parentheses is to show that the harsh usage of the body, and all the teaching of the seducer, was for (or 'as to') the satisfaction of the flesh; 'a certain honour' is what is due to the body.
death (a-3) The aorist. 'be in the state of having done it.' desire, (b-20) Or 'covetousness;' as Eph. 4.19 ('greedy unsatisfied lust'), and Eph. 5.5 ('unbridled lust').
which (c-2) Or 'among whom.'
off, (a-4) The aorist. 'be in the state of having done it.'

new, (d-6) Neos, i.e. young or fresh. see Luke 5.37, Heb. 12.24. renewed (e-7) Renewed -- the present tense -- is from the same root as kainos, as in Rom. 12.2; 2Cor. 4.16; Tit. 3.5; and refers to what is entirely new in contrast to old.
everything, (f-18) Lit. 'all things,' as 1Cor. 15.28.
on (a-2) The aorist. 'be in the state of having done it.'
forgiving (g-5) forgiven (g-21) As Eph. 4.32.

wisdom (h-13) It is a question of spiritual understanding whether 'in all wisdom' relates to 'dwell' or to 'teaching.' It may be the former. Paul taught in all wisdom (ch. 1.28), and in them the word was so to dwell. psalms, (i-20) 'In psalms,' &c., may be connected with 'singing' rather than with what precedes. but in Eph. 5.19, 'speaking' is connected with 'psalms.'
heartily, (k-7) Ek psuches. lit. 'from the soul.'
serve (a-15) Douleuo, serve as a bondman, see Note, 1Cor. 4.1.
opportunities. (b-8) See Note, Eph. 5.16.
minister (c-7) Diakonos, ver. 17 diakonia. see Note, 1Cor. 4.1.
who (d-20) 'Who are such as have been.'
complete (e-30) Or, possibly, 'fully assured,' as ch. 2.2; 1Thess. 1.5; Heb. 6.11; 10.22. will (f-34) Lit. 'in every will of God,' everything that is such.
ministry (c-9) Diakonos, ver. 17 diakonia. see Note, 1Cor. 4.1. fulfil (g-22) Pleroo, as ch. 1.9, and 'complete,' ch. 1.25; 2.10.
